rows.text: I want to build a local-first app for audio interviews: searchable transcripts, speaker labels, clips with notes. Nothing leaves the laptop.
Love it. The hard parts are speaker labels, word-level timing and long recordings on an ordinary laptop. I'd scope v1 to one flow: import an interview, find a passage, save a clip with a note.
Sounds right. Let's /jumpstart this and see if we can start from a solid open-source base.

items.text: Read Scriberr's code at a pinned commit

rows.text: Someone already built most of this.
**Scriberr** (MIT) already does offline transcription, speaker labels, click-to-jump and notes pinned to a time range.
**Extend Scriberr** (recommended). You add search inside transcripts and clip export.
**Extend noScribe** (GPL-3.0). Built for interviews; library, search and clips are still yours to build.
**Compose WhisperX + pyannote.** Full control, but the whole app is yours to build.
I'd start with A. Want me to set it up?
